text:
The loudest story in Philadelphia belongs to Matvei Michkov. He has spent two weeks in trade-rumor headlines, from "Will Matvei Michkov stay with the Flyers for the entire season?" to a piece on the front office drawing a line for teammates, and Rick Tocchet said the team has handled the noise "really well" while acknowledging it is there. The hockey has been louder lately: a four-game point streak, projected ice time up to 18:43 from 16:28 on the season, and a place as our sleeper tonight at 61% for a point, well above his season pace. Travis Konecny's own future is now a talking point too, with Daily Faceoff asking whether a divorce would suit both sides, while Charlie O'Connor posted that one report "doesn't pass the smell test."

The Flyers need every bit of it. They are at 18 points with a 4% playoff chance in our simulations and a minus-23 goal difference. Some of that is finishing, 11.7 goals below what their chances usually produce, but they also take just 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) at five on five. Sunday's 5-2 loss to Edmonton came with 75% of the chances and an 0-for-8 power play, which tells you both halves of their season. Joseph Woll starts at .902 and plus-5.1. Denver Barkey, two goals including the winner against Columbus last week, is cleared to play.

Buffalo is in its own hole: winless in four, outscored 17-6, after an 8-3 home loss to Tampa in which Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled. Alex Lyon gets the start over Luukkonen, who has 12 of the 20 starts, and Joe Yerdon noted Lyon has been blunt about where the team stands. The Sabres' chances are about even, and 9.3 goals of missing finish explain much of their minus-14. Tage Thompson is one assist from 200 for his career.

Our numbers have Buffalo a shade ahead, 3.04 expected goals to 2.93. Philadelphia won the first meeting 3-1 in October, a game it deserved 48% of the time.
headline: Michkov noise, Sabres slide, and Lyon in net
